- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.6) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to match sentiment momentum.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.4), model often overcorrects downward — adjust upward to avoid excessive bearish bias.  
- Model frequently underestimates sharp upward moves (especially after sentiment spikes) — add a small lagged momentum buffer to forecast.  
- Model overestimates downward corrections after recent highs — reduce forecast by 5–10% if sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.  
- Mean reversion is overemphasized — if forecast is 10%+ below recent 5-day average, adjust upward slightly to avoid premature reversal.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period spikes — add a 1–2 day lagged sentiment-weighted adjustment to the final 5–7 days.
